title: atomic release staging, Helm preflight hooks, and compressed release manifests for safer private-installer rollouts
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: private on‑prem/VPC upgrades require greater atomicity and preflight validation to avoid partial rollouts and long rollback windows. This PR introduces a small release staging layer, Helm preflight hooks (pre-install/pre-upgrade/validate), and a compact compression/packing step for release manifests and provenance files so that the installer can stage an entire release snapshot atomically and validate it before switching the live release pointer. Design summary: 1) release-stager: an ephemeral staging area in S3/GCS with an atomic 'active' pointer object; publish pipeline uploads a packed, signed archive and a JSON index; after successful post-signature validations the pipeline atomically swaps a symlink-style object (bucket key replace) to make the new release active; 2) manifest packing: index_pack.go creates deterministic tar stream, zstd compresses blobs with level 3 for speed, and the pack includes SHA256 provenance metadata for each entry to simplify verification during installs; 3) Helm preflight hooks: small Helm hooks run before install/upgrade to validate node resources, image accessibility, KMS availability, and required CRDs; failures are surfaced early and abort the Helm transaction; 4) installer/rollback: upgrade tool gains a two-phase apply with an automatic dry-run validation and a deterministic rollback plan derived from the staged index so rollbacks are fast and do not rely on ad-hoc heuristics. CI changes: new pipeline job ci/pipelines/release-stager.yml validates packing/compression, runs signature verification, and performs a smoke deploy to minikube in under 6 minutes. Security: signing routine ensures reproducible tar order before cosign signing and inserts a small attestation with build-info and builder git-ref. Backwards compatibility: published archives include both packed zstd artifact and legacy uncompressed blobs to allow older private-installer clients to continue fetching if necessary; rollout plan includes a two-week dual-read window before deprecating legacy path. Testing: unit tests for packer and signature validator, integration tests for staged swap and Helm preflight, and manual canary in a staging VPC. Rollout: merge -> pipeline produces staged artifact -> run canary promotion job -> after 24h and monitoring approval, auto-swap active pointer for production. See release_notes for more details and migration steps.
commits: feat(stager): add release-stager pipeline and bucket pointer swap
feat(pack): deterministic tar packing and zstd compression for release manifests
feat(helm): add pre-install and pre-upgrade preflight hooks
fix(ci): tolerate transient object-not-found during atomic swap retry
test(ci): add minikube smoke test for staged release install
chore(docs): document staged release promotion and rollback steps
review_conversation: Diego Ramirez: Great direction — two questions: (1) how do we guarantee the atomic swap across S3/GCS and avoid partial reads during swap? (2) can we keep a short-lived dual-read window by default?

Asha Patel: Response: swap implemented by an object-replace with versioned buckets and a linearizable head object; we add a small retry backoff (100ms) during installs to handle eventual consistency edge-cases. Dual-read window set to 48h by default configurable via TF module.
Sophie Nguyen: Can we validate KMS availability earlier? Helm hook runs a KMS health-check and fails fast; added unit tests for simulating KMS timeout.
Evelyn Clark: Nit: packer code needs a deterministic file ordering comment and a test. Addressed in commit 'test(pack): add deterministic-order test'
Diego Ramirez: CI failure on first run (integration timeout) — re-run fixed it and logs show transient minikube image pull issue. Verified in subsequent run. Approved after green CI.
ci_summary: Pipeline: release-stager (pack -> sign -> verify) passed; e2e minikube smoke test passed; linters passed. First CI run timed out on minikube image pull, rerun was green.
release_notes:
- Introduces atomic release staging: publishes a packed, signed artifact and atomically swaps the active release pointer in object storage.
- Adds deterministic packing and zstd compression for release manifests and provenance, reducing release size and improving upload latency.
- Adds Helm preflight hooks (pre-install, pre-upgrade) to validate cluster preconditions and abort unsafe rollouts.
- Upgrade tool now generates a deterministic rollback plan from staged indexes to make rollbacks reliable and fast.
- Backwards compatibility: staged artifacts include legacy uncompressed blobs for a configurable dual-read window.
- CI: new release-stager pipeline with minikube smoke test and signature validation.
testing_notes: Unit: packer deterministic order, zstd roundtrip, signature verify. Integration: staged swap + Helm preflight on minikube. Manual: canary promoted to staging VPC and monitored for 48 hours before prod promotion.
migration_instructions: 1) Operators: update terraform module for release bucket to enable versioning and object-lock suggested setting. 2) If you run on very old installer clients: keep legacy-read enabled (env RELEASE_LEGACY_READ=true) until clients are upgraded. 3) To opt into atomic swap immediately, set release_stager_enabled = true in tf module and run apply. 4) To roll back a staged release: use tools/upgrade/plan_and_rollback --release <name> --rollback-to <timestamp> which calculates deterministic steps from the packed index.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative about compression level to prioritize install speed on constrained customer networks. We plan to introduce optional higher compression for air-gapped distribution in a follow-up change.
notes_for_oncall: If a production install reports 'manifest-signature-mismatch' after promotion, fall back to previous active pointer (stager.undo_swap) and open SUP ticket; artifacts remain in the staging bucket for forensic analysis.
changelog_entry: installer: atomic release staging, deterministic manifest packing, Helm preflight hooks, and deterministic rollback plans (Asha Patel)
